diagnostic_evidence.quote: The collection of intervals produced is pairwise disjoint, each interval $[a_{m,n}(A),b_{m,n}(A)]$ intersects $\spec(A)$, and the union of the intervals covers $\spec(A)$.
If $\Xi_{\mathrm{cc}}(A)<\infty$, then $\spec(A)$ is a finite union of compact intervals. In this case, since $\Gamma_n^\spec(A)\rightarrow\spec(A)$, $M_n(A)\geq \Xi_{\mathrm{cc}}(A)$ for large $n$.

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed inequality $M_n(A)\leq \Xi_{\mathrm{cc}}(A)$ is false: a single cover interval can meet several connected components of $\spec(A)$ (e.g. $[-0.1,3.1]$ covers $[0,1]\cup[2,3]$), and for large $n$ it is the small error bound, not the disjointness/intersection hypotheses alone, that forces one interval per component. Thus the stated argument does not prove $M_n(A)\to\Xi_{\mathrm{cc}}(A)$, although the conclusion is true.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing local argument: for large $n$, $E_n^{\spec}$ is smaller than half the minimum gap between components of $\spec(A)$, so no cover interval can intersect two components and each component is covered by exactly one interval; hence $M_n(A)=\Xi_{\mathrm{cc}}(A)$ for large $n$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the $\Sigma_1^A$ classification of the number of connected components is incomplete; the corollary \texttt{cor_assumI_lims} is not justified by the given argument, though its statement remains true.
issues.title: False upper bound on cover interval count for connected components
issues.why_classification: The repair is short and routine, and the conclusion and algorithm are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Subsequent levels are obtained by taking successive limits in each of these indices. (Since the algorithms at level 2 and beyond result from taking one or more infinite limits, these methods, in principle, can access infinite data.)
Moreover, by the consistency of general algorithms, $\Gamma_{n_k}(\{\Gamma_m^\spec(H_{f_1+\cdots+ f_k})\})=\Gamma_{n_k}(\{\Gamma_m^\spec(H_{f})\})$ for all $k\in\mathbb{N}$.

issues.failure_explanation: In a $\Delta_2^G$ tower the objects $\Gamma_{n_1},\Gamma_{n_2}$ are level-2 algorithms obtained as limits of level-1 general algorithms and may depend on infinitely many cover values $\Gamma_m^\spec$. The proof asserts finite dependence and then applies consistency of general algorithms to equate $\Gamma_{n_k}$ on the constructed and limiting inputs; this inference is invalid, so the alternating $\leq 1/4$ / $\geq 3/4$ contradiction is not established.

failure_location.quote: However, $\Gamma_{n_1}(\{\Gamma_m^\spec(H_{f_1})\})$ can only depend on $\{\Gamma_m^\spec(H_{f_1})\}_{m=1}^{N_1}$ for some finite $N_1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the exact-equality step by a standard diagonal approximation: for each level-2 output $\Gamma_{n_k}$, approximate it by level-1 outputs $\Gamma_{n_k,n}$ for sufficiently large $n$, choose the next perturbation $f_{k+1}$ to match the finitely many cover values used by those level-1 outputs to within a small $\epsilon$, and use the $1/2$ gap between the $1/4$ and $3/4$ bounds to force non-convergence.
issues.overall_effect: The lower bound $\{\mathrm{dim}_{\mathrm{H}}(\spec(\cdot)),\Omega_{\mathrm{DS}}^{\mathrm{(S1)}},[0,1],\Lambda_{\mathrm{(S1)}}\}\notin\Delta_2^G$ is unproven as written, so the advertised optimality of the $\Sigma_2^A$ Hausdorff-dimension algorithm is unsupported.
issues.title: Level-2 algorithms treated as finitely dependent in Hausdorff-dimension lower bound
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained but nontrivial modification of the same diagonal construction; the theorem statement and the $\Sigma_2^A$ upper bound survive, so the loss is not major.

issues.failure_explanation: \cref{lem:cover1} gives eventual constancy of $\widetilde{\Gamma}_{n,m}$ in $m$ for each fixed $n$, but the stabilization threshold can depend on $n$ because the grid $G_{1/2^n,L}$ grows and no uniform convergence rate for $\Phi_m$ is assumed. The claimed $n$-independent $M$ is therefore unjustified; the subsequent max-limit equality is still valid, but only by a different argument using eventual constancy for each fixed $k$.

failure_location.quote: \cref{lem:cover1}'s proof shows there exists $M\in\mathbb{N}$ with $\widetilde{\Gamma}_{n,m}(A)\subset\widetilde{\Gamma}_{n,m+1}(A)$ for all $m\geq M$, independent of $n$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the uniform-$M$ assertion by the correct statement that for each fixed $k$, $\widetilde{\Gamma}_{k+1,n_1}$ is eventually constant in $n_1$, so the ratio is eventually constant and the displayed max-limit equality follows.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the $\Pi_2^A$ classification of the upper box-counting dimension under \textbf{(S2)} contains an unsupported claim, but the classification itself is valid.
issues.title: Unjustified uniform stabilization threshold in upper box-counting proof under (S2)
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-sentence correction and the result is unchanged.
